---
title: "papercraft-nester"
subtitle: "Plan a cut layout around the cardstock you actually have"
---

`papercraft-nester` takes the editable piece groups from a `lowpoly-pdf-to-svg` pattern and packs
them onto a finite inventory of cardstock sheets. It exports one SVG master with an Inkscape page
for each physical sheet, preserving each piece's outline, folds, labels, ID, and material.

The tool is intended to help answer practical questions before cutting: how many sheets of each
colour are needed, how much of each sheet is used, and how much repositioning might the new layout
save. The [guide](guide.qmd) walks through a Bowser run; [methods](methods.qmd) explains how the
placement search works and where it can fall back to the source layout.

## Quick start

From the nester repository root, install it and run the Bowser example from a models repository
that contains the converter output and manifest:

```sh
python -m pip install -e .
papercraft-nester nest \
  --svg ../../data/bowser/bowser.svg \
  --manifest ../../data/bowser/bowser.yaml \
  --inventory config/bowser-letter.json \
  --output output/bowser-letter-master.svg
```

See the [full guide](guide.qmd) for setup, inventory changes, options, and Cricut handoff notes.

## What it preserves

- Each complete piece moves as a unit, keeping its cut path, mountain and valley folds, labels,
  piece ID, and cardstock material together.
- The inventory specifies sheet dimensions and quantity per material, so the packer cannot use
  more stock than is available.
- The output is a multi-page SVG master, with one Inkscape page per sheet.

The optimizer uses deterministic placement heuristics. Its result is a useful layout candidate,
not a proof that no better arrangement exists. Glue tabs are retained intact in the current mode.
